T.topic_fa: میلتون هرشی تبلیغ نمی‌کرد و می‌گفت «کیفیت بهترین تبلیغ است». حالا شرکتش زندگی او را به یک فیلم سینمایی تبدیل کرده: منتقدها می‌گویند یک آگهی طولانی است، تماشاگرها دوستش دارند
T.topic_en: Milton Hershey refused to advertise. 'Give them quality. That's the best kind of advertising.' Now his company has turned his life into a feature film in cinemas: critics call it product placement, audiences love it
T.central_tension_fa: مردی که تبلیغ را قبول نداشت، حالا خودش تبلیغ شده؛ ولی تماشاگرها برای دیدنش بلیت می‌خرند. مردم از آگهی فرار می‌کنند، اما برای یک داستان پول می‌دهند. فرق آگهی و داستان، همان فرق «ما بهترینیم» و «من شکست خوردم» است.
T.central_tension_en: The man who wouldn't advertise is now the ad, and people buy tickets to watch it. We skip ads but pay for stories. The line between them is the line between 'we're the best' and 'I went broke, twice'.
T.working_hook_fa: هرشی تبلیغ نمی‌کرد. حالا مردم برای دیدن تبلیغش بلیت سینما می‌خرند.
T.working_hook_en: Hershey's founder refused to advertise. Now people buy cinema tickets to watch his ad.

key_sources.claim: Film hits theaters Wednesday (25 Nov); Hershey's Suzanne Jones: 'We wanted to make sure this was not in any way, shape or form a 90-minute commercial.' Tie-ins: bars sold via Amazon and Walmart at their original 5-cent price, limited-edition vintage-inspired packaging with QR codes, in-store displays; film and America 250 expected to add almost one point to 2026 sales.

Dandelion Media production in partnership with the Hershey entities; Hershey reviewed scripts and was on set; 'We knew this must not be a 90-minute commercial.' Debuts in theaters nationwide 25 November.

Tomatometer 17% (18 reviews), Popcornmeter 90% (100+ verified ratings); Hollywood Reporter (Frank Scheck): 'essentially serves as a feature-length product placement'. Director Mark Waters; Finn Wittrock as Milton Hershey; distributed by Angel Studios; PG, 1h 48m.

Philadelphia shop (1876) failed six years later; a New York attempt also failed; fresh-milk caramels succeeded; sold the caramel company in 1900 for $1,000,000; the company grew 'despite Hershey's refusal to advertise its products'.
'His first two candy companies were met with failure'; first business ended in bankruptcy; 1918: gave his entire fortune to the Hershey School Trust.
Hershey quote: 'Give them quality. That's the best kind of advertising in the world.'; borrowed $150 from an aunt to open the 1876 shop.

T.framing_note: Type 3 (secret behind a familiar brand) with a 2-day-old news spark (film released 25 Nov). Spine: (1) Hook: the founder refused to advertise; now people buy tickets to watch his ad. (2) His own line: 'Give them quality. That's the best kind of advertising in the world.' (3) The hidden story: his first two candy businesses failed (Philadelphia 1876, ended in bankruptcy; New York also failed). (4) Fresh-milk caramels worked; in 1900 he sold the caramel company for $1 million and bet it on chocolate. (5) He left his fortune to a school trust (1918). (6) This week: the company's life story of him is a feature film in cinemas; the company helped shape the story, and bars are sold at the original 5-cent price with vintage packaging. (7) The split: critics 17%, audiences 90% (as of 27 Nov, small samples: 18 reviews / 100+ ratings — say 'early scores'). The Hollywood Reporter calls it feature-length product placement. (8) Lesson: people skip ads but pay for stories; the story people pay for is the failure, not the boast. Your brand's best ad might be the part you hide. Rules: say 'his company helped make' / 'made with the company', not 'Hershey funded' (no source states funding); say 'early scores', never 'hit' or 'box-office success' (no box office figures found); never claim the 5-cent price lasted X years (no source read); founding year of the caramel company conflicts (1883/1886) — don't put a year on screen for it; one number on screen (17% vs 90% counts as one comparison, or $1 million — pick one per reel). No actor faces generated; real stills/poster only from owner uploads. AI never draws the Hershey logo or wrapper. Distinguish from 2026-11-01 (borrowed fame/sponsorship) and 2026-11-08 (AI ads): this is about story vs. advertising. Never name the UAE, Dubai or any emirate.
